q: Which single-celled organism is added to bread dough to make it rise?
note: The yeast feeds on sugars in the dough and gives off gas, inflating thousands of tiny bubbles in the gluten.

q: What is the process by which green plants use sunlight to make their own food called?
note: The by-product is the oxygen we breathe, which plants release as waste.

q: Chocolate is made from the roasted seeds of which tree?
note: The seeds grow inside large pods straight out of the trunk and taste bitter until they are fermented and roasted.

q: Which pair of organs filters waste out of the blood to produce urine?
note: They process the body's entire blood supply many times a day, keeping salt and water in balance as they go.

q: What is the medical name for the collarbone?
note: It is the most commonly broken bone in the body, because it takes the force of almost any fall onto the shoulder.

q: What is the name for precipitation that falls from a thunderstorm as lumps of ice?
note: Strong updraughts carry the stones up and down through freezing cloud layers, adding a new coat of ice each time.

q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
note: A newborn is about the size of a jellybean and crawls unaided into the pouch to finish developing.

q: Glass is made by melting which common material, found on most beaches?
note: Soda and lime are added to bring the melting point down to something a furnace can reach.

q: What is the largest living species of bird?
note: It cannot fly, but it can outrun a racehorse and lays the largest egg of any living bird.

q: Chopping an onion makes you cry because it releases a gas containing which element, the same one behind the smell of rotten eggs?
note: The sulfur compound reacts with the fluid on your eye to form a mild acid, and tears are the body flushing it away.

q: Honey can sit for thousands of years without spoiling because it contains very little of which substance that microbes need in order to grow?
note: Honey is also naturally acidic, so the little moisture there is gets drawn out of any bacteria that land in it.

q: Yoghurt is made by adding live bacteria to milk, which thicken it by turning milk sugar into which acid?
note: The acid makes the milk proteins clump together, which is what gives yoghurt both its set texture and its tang.

q: Which compound gives chilli peppers their heat?
note: Capsaicin does not dissolve in water, which is why a glass of milk douses the burn far better than a glass of water.

q: Veins often look blue through the skin, but what colour is the deoxygenated blood inside them actually?
note: Human blood is never blue; veins only look that way because of how skin absorbs and scatters the light coming back out.

q: A rhinoceros horn is made of the same protein as human hair and fingernails. What is that protein?
note: Unlike antlers or cattle horns, a rhino's horn has no bone core at all, so a broken one can grow back.

q: Sharks and rays have skeletons made of what, rather than bone?
note: Cartilage is lighter and more flexible than bone, which helps a shark stay buoyant without a swim bladder.

q: Knocking your funny bone is painful because you have actually struck which nerve?
note: It is nothing to do with bone: at the elbow the nerve runs right at the surface with almost no muscle or fat to shield it.

q: Which human organ is able to regrow itself after a large part of it has been removed?
note: This is what makes living donor transplants possible, since both the donated piece and what remains can grow back.

q: Which egg-laying Australian mammal has a duck-like bill and webbed feet?
note: The males also carry venomous spurs on their hind legs, making it one of the few venomous mammals.

q: Flamingos are not born pink. Where does their colour come from?
note: Chicks hatch grey and only turn pink as pigments from the algae and small crustaceans they eat build up in their feathers.

q: Dolphins hunt in murky water by making clicks and listening for the echoes. What is this ability called?
note: The returning echoes are detailed enough to tell a dolphin the size, shape and even the texture of something it cannot see.

q: Sound travels fastest through which of these three: air, water or steel?
note: Most people pick air, but sound moves faster the stiffer the material, so it races through steel roughly fifteen times quicker.

q: Which tree-dwelling mammal of Central and South America is famous for being the slowest-moving mammal?
note: Its leaf diet yields so little energy that a meal can take weeks to digest, and algae grows in its fur.

q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
note: Unlike bone, enamel has no living cells, so once it is worn away the body cannot replace it.

q: Which transparent part of the eye is the only part of the human body with no blood supply of its own?
note: Blood vessels would spoil the view, so the cornea takes oxygen straight from the air and nutrients from tears.

q: A starfish has no blood. What does it pump around its body instead?
note: Seawater is drawn in through a sieve-like plate on its back and used to work the hundreds of tube feet underneath.

q: What single word describes animals such as rabbits and deer that are most active at dawn and dusk?
note: The half light is a decent compromise: enough to see by, but poor hunting conditions for many predators.

q: A potato is not a root. It is a swollen underground example of which other plant part?
note: The eyes are the giveaway: they are buds, and only stems grow buds, which is why a potato can sprout.

q: Dropped from the same height in a vacuum, which reaches the ground first: a hammer or a feather?
accept: They land at the same time
note: Air resistance is the only thing that slows the feather; with no air, gravity accelerates every object at exactly the same rate.

q: The spice cloves are the dried, unopened what of a tropical evergreen tree?
note: Picked once they turn pink and dried until brown, they are the only common spice that is a whole unopened flower.
